note: Hand-curated, sourced entries. Democratic primary contested (Markey vs. Moulton); primary Sept 1, 2026.

MA-senate.statusNote: Sen. Ed Markey won the Sep 1 Democratic primary with 76% over Rep. Seth Moulton, who conceded. John Deaton, the only Republican on the primary ballot, is the GOP nominee. Joseph Tache (Party for Socialism and Liberation) and independent Morgan Dawicki have also filed for the November ballot. Both Tache (Party for Socialism and Liberation) and Dawicki (Independent) confirmed on the Nov 3, 2026 general ballot per Ballotpedia's MA Senate race page, alongside American Independent Party candidate Philip Devincentis and Shiva Ayyadurai (checked Sep 2, 2026).

MA-governor.statusNote: Gov. Maura Healey (D) is seeking a second term and had no primary opponent. Michael Minogue, an Army veteran and former Abiomed CEO, won the Sep 1 Republican primary 76 to 24 over Brian Shortsleeve. Independents Andrea James and Muhammed Kokonezis-Hanino have also filed for the November ballot. Field confirmed by CommonWealth Beacon's Sep 1, 2026 primary coverage and the Wikipedia 2026 Massachusetts gubernatorial election page.

candidates.name: Ed Markey
candidates.background: U.S. Senator since 2013 after 37 years representing Massachusetts in the House; son of a Malden milkman who worked as an ice cream man to pay for college. Senate author of the Green New Deal and a longtime progressive on climate and telecommunications policy. Seeking a third full term at age 80 while facing a primary challenge from Rep. Seth Moulton.
priorities: Bold climate action and clean energy investment
Expand healthcare access and hold corporations accountable

cost.label: Co-authored the Freedom to Move Act offering $5 billion in annual grants for fare-free transit (Wikipedia)

health.label: One of 16 senators to cosponsor the 2017 Medicare for All Act expanding Medicare to all residents (Wikipedia)

housing.label: Co-led the Green New Deal for Public Housing Act: $234 billion for public housing and repeal of the Faircloth Amendment to allow new public housing construction (Markey Senate office)

immigration.label: Co-sponsored the Protecting Sensitive Locations Act limiting ICE enforcement at schools and hospitals; backed protecting military family members from deportation (Wikipedia)

taxes.label: Equal Tax Act co-lead: 'requiring millionaires and billionaires to pay taxes on investment income the same way working people pay taxes on their earnings' (Rep. Ramirez press release)

climate.label: Senate author of the Green New Deal calling for '100% renewable, zero-emission energy sources' (Wikipedia)

education.label: Supports universal preschool for 3- and 4-year-olds; co-sponsored the Child Care for Working Families Act (Wikipedia)

safety.label: Campaign pledges to 'invest in prevention' and 'ensure a fair, just system for all' (campaign site)

repro.label: Opposes abortion restrictions; wore an abortion rights pin to the 2023 State of the Union (Wikipedia)

democracy.label: 'We need to abolish the filibuster for the sake of democracy and pass voting rights legislation', backing the Freedom to Vote: John R. Lewis Act (Markey Senate office)

controversies.label: Faces calls to retire due to age; he will be 80 at the time of the election and Moulton has made generational change the center of his challenge (Wikipedia)

sources.label: MA Secretary of State: 2026 Democratic primary candidates

candidates.name: Seth Moulton
candidates.background: U.S. Representative for Massachusetts's 6th district since 2015; Marine Corps captain who served four tours in Iraq and earned two Bronze Stars with valor. Harvard physics graduate with an MBA/MPA. Announced his primary challenge to Sen. Markey in October 2025, arguing for 'a new generation of leadership' and citing Markey's age.
priorities: American Affordability Agenda: housing, healthcare, and education as human rights
A new generation of leadership in the Senate

cost.label: Affordability Agenda extends prescription drug price caps to all plans, offers mortgage assistance, and frames 'housing, healthcare and education are human rights' (campaign site)

health.label: Backs a 'national public option to lower premiums', extended ACA subsidies, and restricting pharmacy benefit managers (campaign site)

housing.label: Mixed approach: ban private equity from buying homes and strengthen renter protections, alongside building via infill development and ADUs (campaign site)

immigration.label: Campaign publishes a Know Your Rights guide for ICE encounters: 'ICE needs a valid warrant signed by a judge to enter your home' (campaign site)

taxes.label: Funds his agenda with 'a national wealth tax on mega-millionaires and by closing tax loopholes', projected to raise over $3.5 trillion in ten years (campaign site)

climate.label: Supports carbon pricing, banning fossil fuel extraction on federal lands, renewable expansion plus nuclear; signed onto the Green New Deal in 2018 (Wikipedia)

education.label: Universal pre-K for all 4-year-olds and expanded free community college and vocational training (campaign site)

safety.label: Author of the law creating the national 988 mental health crisis line and sponsor of the Brandon Act on military mental health reporting (Wikipedia)

repro.label: Affordability Agenda 'codifies abortion protections' and expands maternal care funding (campaign site)

democracy.label: Would prohibit federal agents at polling places, protect election officials from intimidation, and fund election cybersecurity (campaign site)

controversies.label: Returned $120,000 in AIPAC donations citing the group's support for Netanyahu, though reports said he retained over $40,000; his November 2024 comments on transgender athletes drew backlash he later walked back (Wikipedia)

sources.label: MA Secretary of State: 2026 Democratic primary candidates

candidates.name: John Deaton
candidates.now: Trial attorney and Marine Corps veteran
candidates.background: Trial attorney and Marine Corps Major (medically retired) who grew up in generational poverty in Highland Park, Michigan, and was the only member of his family to finish high school. Nationally known for representing over 75,000 XRP token holders against the SEC. Lost the 2024 Senate race to Elizabeth Warren 60 to 40 after winning the GOP primary with 64.5%; he is the only Republican on the 2026 primary ballot.
priorities: Housing affordability: build five million new homes in five years
Patients Before Profits healthcare reform targeting PBMs
Term limits and government reform (Clean Hands Initiative)

cost.label: Blames government spending for inflation harming working families; would control federal spending and eliminate 'wasteful and unnecessary pork-barrel spending' (Ballotpedia)

health.label: 'Patients Before Profits' plan: ban secret PBM rebates, end PBM-insurer-pharmacy vertical integration, expand telehealth across state lines (campaign site)

housing.label: Build five million homes in five years by cutting federal and state red tape and reforming zoning so private construction can build (campaign site)

immigration.label: Pledged to 'secure the border, end catch and release, and fight to reform the asylum process, while expanding legal immigration' (Ballotpedia)

taxes.label: Backs tax relief, citing 65% voter support for an income tax cut, paired with his pledge to rein in federal spending (campaign site)

climate.label: Opposed the Green New Deal; supports clean energy transition 'without punishing American workers' through 'reasonable sustainable growth' (Ballotpedia)

repro.label: Pro-choice: supports codifying Roe v. Wade and pledged to leave the Republican Party if the GOP pursues a national abortion ban (Axios)

candidates.name: Maura Healey
candidates.now: Governor of Massachusetts since 2023, seeking a second term; ran unopposed in the Democratic primary.
candidates.background: Former Massachusetts Attorney General (2015-2023); first elected governor in 2022 with Lt. Gov. Kim Driscoll as running mate.
priorities: Lowering housing and child care costs

cost.label: Proposed a child tax credit that would give "more than 700,000 families... $600 per child" to help with costs (Ballotpedia, 2022 campaign)

housing.label: 2026 platform commits to "dramatically increasing production, preserving existing housing stock" through zoning reform and state land use, a mix of building more and protecting existing affordability (Ballotpedia)

taxes.label: Signed a tax relief package cutting capital gains taxes and raising the estate tax threshold alongside a middle-class child tax credit (Feb-Oct 2023) (Wikipedia: Maura Healey)

climate.label: Signed an executive order creating a cabinet-level Office of Climate Innovation and Resilience (Jan 2023) and a bill accelerating clean-energy deployment (Dec 2024) (Wikipedia: Maura Healey)

education.label: Proposed and funded the MassReconnect free community college program for residents 25+ (Mar 2023, funded in the 2024 budget) (Wikipedia: Maura Healey)

safety.label: Advocates ending mandatory minimum sentences for nonviolent drug offenders in favor of treatment over incarceration (Wikipedia: Maura Healey)

repro.label: Platform focuses on "expanding access to abortion services" regardless of location, employment, or income (Ballotpedia)

candidates.name: Joseph Tache
candidates.now: Boston youth worker and community organizer running as the Party for Socialism and Liberation candidate against Sen. Ed Markey.
candidates.background: Tache has over a decade of activist experience in Boston, including organizing work with the Party for Socialism and Liberation. He is running an explicitly socialist campaign framed around wealth redistribution and confronting what he calls billionaire hoarding of resources. He is confirmed on the November 3, 2026 general ballot alongside Markey, Republican John Deaton, and independent Morgan Dawicki.
priorities: Capping rent at 10 percent of income
Defending immigrant families and ending deportations

cost.label: Frames high prices as systemic, arguing "billionaires hoard wealth while workers struggle" (tache4ma.com platform)

health.label: Platform calls for "guaranteeing free healthcare" as part of meeting people's essential needs (tache4ma.com platform)

housing.label: Central plank calls for "capping rent at 10% of income" (tache4ma.com platform)

immigration.label: "Defend Immigrant Families, End Deportations," opposes "scapegoating immigrants" (tache4ma.com platform)

taxes.label: Calls for "seizing the top 100 corporations" and redistributing wealth (tache4ma.com platform)

climate.label: "Only with working people in power can we implement real climate solutions," framed as systemic change (tache4ma.com platform)

education.label: Platform includes free education alongside "creating millions of union jobs" (tache4ma.com platform)
